title: What Happens If You Hold Your Breath?
sources: Healthline, 'What happens when you hold your breath' (CO2 build-up drives the urge to breathe; involuntary breathing movements; fainting, after which breathing resumes)
UBC Science Creative Quarterly, 'Waiting to inhale: why it hurts to hold your breath' (CO2 sensing, diaphragm contractions)
Redwoods Group, 'Breath holding and shallow water blackout' (passing out underwater can be fatal)
Mammalian diving reflex: breath-holding slows the heart rate (bradycardia), most strongly with the face in cold water

lines.text: What happens if you hold your breath for as long as you can?
For the first thirty seconds, nothing much.
Your lungs are full, and your blood is still carrying plenty of oxygen.
But carbon dioxide starts building up,
and that, not the lack of oxygen, is what makes you desperate to breathe.
lines.caps: That, *not | lack of *oxygen | makes you *desperate | to *breathe

lines.text: Your diaphragm starts twitching, trying to force a breath,
and your heart actually slows down to save oxygen.
Push even further, and your brain simply switches you off.
You pass out, and your body starts breathing again on its own.
lines.caps: You pass *out | your *body | *breathing again | on its *own

lines.text: Which is why you should never try this underwater.
lines.caps: Which is *why | you should *never | try this *underwater
